summary: A person who saves a tiny amount of something for planting, as a sample, or for medicine, is chayav for carrying even a tiny amount, because it is important to him. Other people are chayav only for the usual amount.

chunks.en: One who saves something for seed, as a sample, or for medicine,
chunks.st: One who stores a seed for sowing, or as a sample, or for medicinal purposes

chunks.en: and carried it out on Shabbos,
chunks.st: and carried it out on Shabbat is

chunks.en: is chayav for any amount.
chunks.st: liable for carrying out any amount.
chunks.stMore: By storing that measure, he indicates that it is significant to him. Therefore, he is liable for carrying it, despite the fact that what he carried out is less than the halakhic measure that determines liability for that item.

chunks.en: But any other person is not chayav
chunks.st: And any other person is

chunks.en: for it except for its full amount.
chunks.st: only liable for carrying it out on Shabbat if he carries out its measure
chunks.stMore: for liability. If one stored the seed, carried it out,

chunks.en: If he then brought it back in,
chunks.st: and then brought it back in,
chunks.stMore: with no intention to utilize it for the specific purpose for which he stored it,

chunks.en: he is chayav only for its full amount.
chunks.st: he is only liable if he brought in its measure for liability (Rav Shmuel Strashun).

summary: A person is chayav for carrying only if he does the whole melacha at once. If he put food on the doorstep in between, or left part of a basket inside, he is patur.

chunks.en: One who carries out food and puts it on the doorstep,
chunks.st: One who carries out food from his house on Shabbat and placed it on the threshold of the door,

chunks.he: בֵּין שֶׁחָזַר וְהוֹצִיאָן בֵּין שֶׁהוֹצִיאָן אַחֵר,
chunks.en: whether he went back and carried it out, or someone else carried it out,
chunks.st: whether he then carried it out from the threshold into the public domain or another person carried it out,

chunks.he: פָּטוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה מְלַאכְתּוֹ בְּבַת אֶחָת.
chunks.en: is patur, because he did not do his melacha all at once.
chunks.st: he is exempt because he did not perform his prohibited labor of carrying from domain to domain all at once. Similarly, if one

chunks.en: A basket full of fruit
chunks.st: placed a basket that is full of fruit

chunks.en: that he put on the outer doorstep,
chunks.st: on the outer threshold,
chunks.stMore: which is in the public domain, and part of the basket remained inside,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרֹב הַפֵּרוֹת מִבַּחוּץ,
chunks.en: even though most of the fruit is outside,
chunks.st: even though most of the fruit is outside in the public domain, he is

chunks.he: פָּטוּר, עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיא אֶת כָּל הַקֻּפָּה:
chunks.en: he is patur until he carries out the whole basket.
chunks.st: exempt until he carries out the entire basket.

summary: A person is chayav for carrying out only if he carries the normal way, like in his hand or on his shoulder. If he carries in a strange way, like with his foot or in his shoe, he is patur.

chunks.en: One who carries out, whether in his right hand or in his left,
chunks.st: One who carries out an object into the public domain on Shabbat, whether he carried it out in his right hand or in his left hand, whether he carried it

chunks.en: in his lap or on his shoulder,
chunks.st: in his lap or on his shoulders,

chunks.en: is chayav, because that is how the sons of Kehas carried.
chunks.st: he is liable. All of these are typical methods of carrying out an object, as this was the method of carrying the sacred vessels of the Tabernacle employed by the sons of Kehat in the desert. All labors prohibited on Shabbat are derived from the Tabernacle, including the prohibited labor of carrying out from domain to domain. But one who carries an object out in an unusual,

words.note: A family of Leviim who carried the Mishkan's holy vessels.

chunks.en: With the back of his hand,
chunks.st: backhanded manner, or

chunks.en: with his foot, his mouth, or his elbow,
chunks.st: with his foot, or with his mouth, or with his elbow,

chunks.en: with his ear or with his hair,
chunks.st: with his ear, or with his hair, or

chunks.en: or in his belt with its opening down,
chunks.st: with his belt [punda] whose opening faced downward, or

chunks.en: between his belt and his shirt,
chunks.st: between his belt and his cloak, or

chunks.en: or in the hem of his shirt,
chunks.st: with the hem of his cloak, or

chunks.en: in his shoe or in his sandal,
chunks.st: with his shoe, or with his sandal,

chunks.en: he is patur, because he did not carry the way people carry.
chunks.st: he is exempt because he did not carry it out in a manner typical of those who carry.

summary: If someone planned to carry something in front of him and it ended up behind him, he is patur. A belt or apron can easily turn around, so a woman is chayav either way.

chunks.he: הַמִּתְכַּוֵּן לְהוֹצִיא לְפָנָיו וּבָא לוֹ לְאַחֲרָיו,
chunks.en: One who meant to carry something in front of him, and it ended up behind him,
chunks.st: One who intends to carry out an object with the object before him, and as he was walking the object came to be carried behind him,

chunks.en: is patur. If behind him, and it ended up in front of him,
chunks.st: is exempt. However, if he intended to carry it out behind him and it came to be carried before him,

chunks.en: he is chayav. In truth they said:
chunks.st: he is liable. In truth they said:

chunks.en: A woman who wears an apron, whether
chunks.st: A woman who girded herself in a pants-like sinar worn beneath the outer garments, whether she placed an object

chunks.en: in front of her or behind her, is chayav,
chunks.st: before her or behind her, and it came to be carried on the other side, she is liable,

chunks.en: because it often turns around.
chunks.st: as it is common for the sinar to be reversed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: also the people who carry letters.
chunks.st: Even those royal couriers, who receive notes [pittakin],
chunks.stMore: carry those notes in their belts, and are not particular where on their belt they carry the notes (Rav Hai Gaon), are liable for carrying out the notes whether they carried them before them or behind them.

summary: Who is chayav when two people carry something together, or when something is carried inside a vessel or on a bed? Rabbi Shimon disagrees in some cases.

chunks.en: One who carries a loaf into the street
chunks.st: One who carries a large mass out to the public domain on Shabbat

chunks.en: is chayav. If two people carried it out,
chunks.st: is liable. If two carried it out together,

chunks.he: פְּטוּרִין. לֹא יָכֹל אֶחָד לְהוֹצִיאוֹ וְהוֹצִיאוּהוּ שְׁנַיִם,
chunks.en: they are patur. If one person could not carry it, and two carried it out,
chunks.st: they are exempt because neither performed a complete prohibited labor. However, if one person is unable to carry it out alone, and therefore two people carried it out,

chunks.en: they are chayav. But Rabbi Shimon says they are patur.
chunks.st: they are liable. And Rabbi Shimon deems them exempt even in that case.

chunks.en: One who carries out less than the amount of food in a vessel
chunks.st: One who carries out foods less than the measure that determines liability for carrying out food in a vessel on Shabbat

chunks.en: is patur even for the vessel,
chunks.st: is exempt, even for carrying out the vessel,

chunks.en: because the vessel is secondary to it.
chunks.st: because the vessel is secondary to
chunks.stMore: the food inside it. Since one is not liable for carrying out the food, he is not liable for carrying out the vessel either. Similarly, one who carries out a

chunks.en: A living person on a bed:
chunks.st: living person on a bed

chunks.en: he is patur even for the bed,
chunks.st: is exempt, even for carrying out the bed,

chunks.en: because the bed is secondary to him.
chunks.st: because the bed is secondary to the person. One who carries out

chunks.en: A dead body on a bed:
chunks.st: a corpse on a bed

chunks.he: חַיָּב. וְכֵן כַּזַּיִת מִן הַמֵּת וְכַזַּיִת
chunks.en: he is chayav. And the same for an olive's size of a dead body, and an olive's size
chunks.st: is liable. And similarly, one who carries out an olive-bulk of a corpse, or an olive-bulk

chunks.en: of a neveilah, and a lentil's size of a sheretz,
chunks.st: of an animal carcass, or a lentil-bulk of a creeping animal,
chunks.stMore: which are the minimal measures of these items that transmit ritual impurity,

words.note: An animal that died without shechitah.
A small creeping animal, like a mouse.

chunks.en: he is chayav. But Rabbi Shimon says he is patur.
chunks.explain: He only wants to get rid of them.
chunks.st: is liable. And Rabbi Shimon deems him exempt.
chunks.stMore: He holds that one is only liable for performing a prohibited labor for its own sake. One who carries out an object in order to bring it to its destination is liable. However, people carry out a corpse or an animal carcass only to be rid of them.

summary: Cutting nails or hair, braiding, or putting on makeup on Shabbos: Rabbi Eliezer says it is a Torah melacha, and the Sages say it is forbidden by the Rabbis. The mishnah also teaches about picking from a plant in a pot.

chunks.en: One who takes off his nails with each other,
chunks.st: one who removes his fingernails with one another on Shabbat without scissors,

chunks.en: or with his teeth,
chunks.st: or with his teeth, and the same is true with regard to one who removes

chunks.en: and the same with his hair,
chunks.st: his hair with his hands, and the same is true with regard to

chunks.en: and the same with his mustache,
chunks.st: his mustache, and the same is true with regard to

chunks.en: and the same with his beard,
chunks.st: his beard, and the same is true with regard to a woman

chunks.en: and the same for a woman who braids her hair,
chunks.st: who braids her hair, and the same is true with regard to one

chunks.en: and the same for one who paints her eyes,
chunks.st: who applies blue eye shadow, and the same is true with regard to one

chunks.en: and the same for one who puts on rouge,
chunks.st: who applies blush,

words.en: the one who puts on rouge

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says they are chayav,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer deems them all liable,
chunks.stMore: as they each performed a labor prohibited by Torah law.

chunks.en: and the Sages forbid it because of a rabbinic rule.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis prohibited performing all of these actions due to rabbinic decree.
chunks.stMore: None of the actions constitute prohibited labors.

chunks.en: One who picks from a pot with a hole
chunks.st: One who severs a leaf or a fruit from a plant growing in a perforated flowerpot on Shabbat

chunks.en: is chayav, and from one without a hole,
chunks.st: is liable, as a plant in a flowerpot with holes in it has the legal status of a plant connected to the ground. Picking from it is prohibited due to reaping. And one who picks from an imperforated pot is

chunks.he: פָּטוּר. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה:
chunks.en: he is patur. And Rabbi Shimon says he is patur in both cases.
chunks.explain: A pot with a hole is like the ground.
chunks.st: exempt, but it is prohibited to do so ab initio. And Rabbi Shimon deems one who does so exempt in both this, the case of the perforated flowerpot, and that, the case of the imperforated flowerpot.
